author: y. r. wisniewski
title: Adam Smith addresses gender pay gap, Middle East conflict, and Trump presidency
text:
Rep. Adam Smith, who represents Washington’s 9th district in the U.S. Congress, recently addressed issues ranging from gender pay disparities to international conflict and national politics in a series of posts on his social media account.
On April 12, Smith highlighted economic challenges faced by women in Washington state, stating: “Unacceptable stats to represent our state. With women earning about $18,500 less than men, the high cost of living makes it even harder for women—especially women of color—to stay in Washington. We need equal pay now.”
Two days later, on April 14, Smith turned his attention to foreign affairs and expressed concern over civilian casualties resulting from military actions in Lebanon. He wrote: “I’ve heard from many constituents who are deeply concerned about the civilian casualties in Lebanon from Israel air strikes. The war in Lebanon must stop and Israel must work with the Lebanese government to strengthen institutions, support stability, and give people a real”.
On April 15, Smith commented on domestic politics regarding former President Donald Trump: “I would be a much happier person if Donald Trump was not the president tomorrow, but we have to think strategically about stopping him.”
Smith has served as a member of Congress since 1997 after succeeding Randy Tate and previously held office in the Washington State Senate from 1991 to 1997. Born in Washington, D.C., in 1965, he currently resides in Bellevue. Smith is an alumnus of Fordham University (BA) and holds a JD from the University of Washington.
